newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM hopes ADRs will attract investors.
newsitem.headline: UPM hopes ADRs will attract investors.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy hopes its American Depositary Receipt (ADR) programme will attract new investors and it has no current plans for a listing on the New York Stock Exchange, a UPM-Kymmene spokesman said.
"Repola had a similar programme and it attracted new investors. We hope this would, too," UPM-Kymmene investor relations officer Kari Toikka told Reuters on Thursday.
"We have no plans (for a listing), if we said we would, from that day, we would have to start living by the rules (of the New York Stock Exchange," he added.

UPM-Kymmene -- formed through the merger of Repola Oy and Kymmene Oy -- on Thursday announced a level-one sponsored ADR programme. The programme introduces trade in dollar terms and this would make it easier for U.S. investors to trade its shares, UPM-Kymmene said in a statement.
Repola's ADR programme, which the merger ended, gave it an estimated 5,000 U.S. shareholders who held some two percent of its shares, UPM-Kymmene said.
Only three Finnish companies are listed on the New York Stock Exchange: Nokia, Valmet and Rauma
